+def _collision_graph(
+    digits: tuple[int, ...], m: int
+) -> dict[tuple[int, ...], tuple[tuple[int, ...], ...]]:
+    """Build the bounded-difference collision graph at aperture ``m``."""
+    if m < 2:
+        raise ValueError("the collision graph requires m>=2")
+    d = digits[0]
+    q = q_sequence(digits, m)
+    modulus = q[m]
+    vertices = product(range(-d, d + 1), repeat=m - 1)
+    adjacency: dict[tuple[int, ...], tuple[tuple[int, ...], ...]] = {}
+    for vertex in vertices:
+        following = []
+        for appended in range(-d, d + 1):
+            weighted = sum(q[j] * vertex[j] for j in range(m - 1))
+            weighted += q[m - 1] * appended
+            if weighted % modulus == 0:
+                following.append(vertex[1:] + (appended,))
+        adjacency[vertex] = tuple(following)
+    return adjacency
+
+
+def _reachable_cycle(
+    adjacency: dict[tuple[int, ...], tuple[tuple[int, ...], ...]],
+    starts: list[tuple[int, ...]],
+) -> tuple[int, ...] | None:
+    """Return the first-coordinate word on a cycle reachable from ``starts``."""
+    color: dict[tuple[int, ...], int] = {}
+    parent: dict[tuple[int, ...], tuple[int, ...]] = {}
+
+    def visit(vertex: tuple[int, ...]) -> tuple[int, ...] | None:
+        color[vertex] = 1
+        for following in adjacency[vertex]:
+            if color.get(following, 0) == 0:
+                parent[following] = vertex
+                witness = visit(following)
+                if witness is not None:
+                    return witness
+            elif color[following] == 1:
+                reverse_cycle = [vertex]
+                while reverse_cycle[-1] != following:
+                    reverse_cycle.append(parent[reverse_cycle[-1]])
+                cycle = tuple(reversed(reverse_cycle))
+                return tuple(state[0] for state in cycle)
+        color[vertex] = 2
+        return None
+
+    for start in starts:
+        if color.get(start, 0) == 0:
+            witness = visit(start)
+            if witness is not None:
+                return witness
+    return None
+
+
+def collision_graph_analysis(
+    digits: tuple[int, ...], m: int
+) -> dict[str, int | bool | tuple[int, ...] | None]:
+    """Return the exact injectivity, causal-depth, and cycle certificates."""
+    adjacency = _collision_graph(digits, m)
+    zero = (0,) * (m - 1)
+    starts = [vertex for vertex in adjacency if vertex[0] != 0]
+    zero_predecessors = [vertex for vertex, targets in adjacency.items() if zero in targets]
+    periodic_witness = _reachable_cycle(adjacency, starts)
+    if periodic_witness is not None and periodic_witness[0] < 0:
+        periodic_witness = tuple(-entry for entry in periodic_witness)
+    injective = periodic_witness is None
+
+    causal_length = None
+    if injective:
+        longest_cache: dict[tuple[int, ...], int] = {}
+
+        def longest_path(vertex: tuple[int, ...]) -> int:
+            if vertex not in longest_cache:
+                longest_cache[vertex] = max(
+                    (1 + longest_path(target) for target in adjacency[vertex]),
+                    default=0,
+                )
+            return longest_cache[vertex]
+
+        causal_length = 1 + max(longest_path(start) for start in starts)
+
+    return {
+        "injective": injective,
+        "causal_length": causal_length,
+        "periodic_witness": periodic_witness,
+        "zero_predecessor_is_unique": zero_predecessors == [zero],
+        "state_bound": len(adjacency) - 1,
+    }
+
+
+def aperture_two_claims(
+    digits: tuple[int, ...],
+) -> dict[str, int | str | tuple[int, ...] | None]:
+    """Classify aperture two by the second-digit boundary parameter."""
+    if len(digits) < 2:
+        raise ValueError("the aperture-two classification requires Parry order p>=2")
+    d = digits[0]
+    boundary = digits[1] + (1 if len(digits) > 2 else 0)
+    analysis = collision_graph_analysis(digits, 2)
+    if boundary == d + 1:
+        regime = "local_bijection"
+    elif boundary == d:
+        regime = "constant_branch_pair"
+    else:
+        regime = "two_output_inverse"
+    return {
+        "boundary_parameter": boundary,
+        "regime": regime,
+        "causal_length": analysis["causal_length"],
+        "periodic_witness": analysis["periodic_witness"],
+    }
+

+\begin{corollary}[Causal completeness and periodic detection]
+\label{cor:simple-parry-causal-completeness}
+Under the preceding hypotheses, for every $m\ge2$ the following are
+equivalent:
+\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\roman*)}]
+  \item $\Phi_{\beta,m}$ is injective;
+  \item $\ell_{\rm cau}(\beta,m)<\infty$;
+  \item no directed cycle of $\Gamma_{\beta,m}$ is reachable from $B$.
+\end{enumerate}
+If these conditions hold, then
+\begin{equation}
+1\le \ell_{\rm cau}(\beta,m)
+\le (2d+1)^{m-1}-1.
+\label{eq:simple-parry-causal-state-bound}
+\end{equation}
+If they fail, there are distinct periodic raw points with the same image and
+with common period at most $(2d+1)^{m-1}-1$.  Thus injectivity in this class
+can be decided by a finite forward cycle search, and every failure has a
+bounded periodic certificate.
+\end{corollary}
+
+\begin{proof}
+The recurrence \eqref{eq:simple-parry-Q} gives $Q_1=d+1$ and shows
+inductively that $Q_n>Q_{n-1}$: before the terminal index there is the
+additional summand $1$, while at and after that index the positive term
+$t_pQ_{n-p}$ accompanies $dQ_{n-1}$.  In particular, $Q_m>d$.
+
+Let $\mathbf0=(0,\ldots,0)\in\Delta_d^{m-1}$.  If an edge
+$v\to\mathbf0$ exists, the overlap conditions give
+$v_1=\cdots=v_{m-2}=0$, and the edge congruence reduces to
+$v_0\equiv0\pmod{Q_m}$.  Since $|v_0|\le d<Q_m$, necessarily
+$v=\mathbf0$.  Hence the zero vertex has the zero vertex as its unique
+predecessor and is not reachable from $B$.
+
+If $\Phi_{\beta,m}$ is injective, the last assertion of
+Theorem~\ref{thm:simple-parry-causal-collision} now gives a finite causal
+inverse.  The converse is immediate because a decoder recovers every raw
+coordinate.  A directed cycle reachable from $B$ cannot contain
+$\mathbf0$; repeating its first-coordinate labels gives a nonzero periodic
+difference sequence and hence, by taking positive and negative parts, two
+distinct periodic raw points with the same image.  Conversely, from any
+nonzero bi-infinite collision path, shift to a vertex in $B$.  Its forward
+path avoids $\mathbf0$ and therefore repeats among the
+$(2d+1)^{m-1}-1$ nonzero vertices, producing a reachable directed cycle.
+This proves all three equivalences and the periodic certificate, whose cycle
+may be chosen simple.
+
+In the injective case the forward subgraph reachable from $B$ is acyclic and
+contains at most $(2d+1)^{m-1}-1$ vertices.  A directed path in it has at
+most $(2d+1)^{m-1}-2$ edges.  Formula
+\eqref{eq:collision-graph-longest-path} then gives
+\eqref{eq:simple-parry-causal-state-bound}.
+\end{proof}
+
+\begin{theorem}[Complete aperture-two trichotomy]
+\label{thm:simple-parry-aperture-two}
+Set
+\[
+c_\beta=t_2+\ind_{\{p\ge3\}}.
+\]
+Then $1\le c_\beta\le d+1$ and
+\[
+Q_2=d(d+1)+c_\beta.
+\]
+Exactly one of the following alternatives holds.
+\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\alph*)}]
+  \item If $c_\beta=d+1$, then $\Fold_{\beta,2}$ is the identity on
+  $\mathcal A_d^2$ and $\ell_{\rm cau}(\beta,2)=1$.
+  \item If $1\le c_\beta<d$, then $\Phi_{\beta,2}$ is injective and
+  $\ell_{\rm cau}(\beta,2)=2$.
+  \item If $c_\beta=d$, then $\Phi_{\beta,2}$ is noninjective.  Its sole
+  nonsingleton path-space fiber is
+  \[
+  \Phi_{\beta,2}(0^{\mathbb Z})
+  =\Phi_{\beta,2}(d^{\mathbb Z})
+  =((0,0))^{\mathbb Z},
+  \]
+  and $\ell_{\rm cau}(\beta,2)=\infty$.
+\end{enumerate}
+For $p=2$ the three cases are determined by $c_\beta=t_2$; for
+$p\ge3$ they are determined by $c_\beta=t_2+1$.  In particular, a binary
+simple-Parry word of order at least three has an identity aperture-two fold
+when $t_2=1$ and exactly the displayed constant branch pair when $t_2=0$.
+\end{theorem}
+
+\begin{proof}
+Put $q=d+1$ and $M=Q_2=dq+c_\beta$.  The formula for $Q_2$ follows directly
+from \eqref{eq:simple-parry-Q}, with the boundary summand $1$ present exactly
+when $2<p$.  Since $t_2\ge1$ when $p=2$, whereas $0\le t_2\le d$ when
+$p\ge3$, the stated range for $c_\beta$ follows.
+
+An edge of $\Gamma_{\beta,2}$ is a pair $(e,f)\in\Delta_d^2$ satisfying
+\begin{equation}
+e+qf\equiv0\pmod M.
+\label{eq:aperture-two-edge-congruence}
+\end{equation}
+The left side has modulus at most
+$d(1+q)=q^2-1<2M$, so it equals $-M$, $0$, or $M$.  If it is zero, then
+$q>|e|$ forces $(e,f)=(0,0)$.  If it is $M$, the bound $e\le d$ forces
+$f=d$, because $f\le d-1$ would give
+$M-qf\ge q+c_\beta>d$; hence $(e,f)=(c_\beta,d)$, which is admissible
+exactly when $c_\beta\le d$.  The case $-M$ is its negative.  Thus the full
+edge set is
+\[
+\{(0,0)\}\quad(c_\beta=d+1),
+\qquad
+\{(0,0),\ \pm(c_\beta,d)\}\quad(c_\beta\le d).
+\]
+
+When $c_\beta=d+1$, one has $Q_2=q^2=|\mathcal A_d^2|$, so every raw
+length-two word is legal and cyclic reduction does nothing.  This proves
+(a).  If $c_\beta<d$, the two nonzero edges cannot be followed by another
+edge, because their terminal vertices are $\pm d$, not $\pm c_\beta$.
+There is a one-output collision but no two-output collision, so
+Theorem~\ref{thm:simple-parry-causal-collision} gives (b).  Finally, when
+$c_\beta=d$, the two nonzero edges are the loops $(d,d)$ and $(-d,-d)$.
+They give precisely the constant difference sequences $\pm d^{\mathbb Z}$.
+The only raw realization of either is the pair
+$\{0^{\mathbb Z},d^{\mathbb Z}\}$, and the common residue is zero in every
+window.  No other nonzero bi-infinite path exists, proving (c) and the fiber
+classification.
+\end{proof}
+

+    def test_injective_folds_have_finite_causal_length_within_state_bound(self):
+        for digits, m, expected_length in (
+            ((1, 1, 1), 4, 2),
+            ((1, 0, 1), 4, 4),
+            ((2, 1), 2, 2),
+            ((2, 0, 1), 2, 2),
+        ):
+            result = collision_graph_analysis(digits, m)
+            self.assertTrue(result["injective"])
+            self.assertEqual(result["causal_length"], expected_length)
+            self.assertLessEqual(result["causal_length"], result["state_bound"])
+            self.assertTrue(result["zero_predecessor_is_unique"])
+            self.assertIsNone(result["periodic_witness"])
+
+    def test_noninjectivity_has_a_bounded_periodic_collision_witness(self):
+        for digits, m in (((1, 0, 1), 3), ((2, 2), 2)):
+            result = collision_graph_analysis(digits, m)
+            witness = result["periodic_witness"]
+            self.assertFalse(result["injective"])
+            self.assertIsNone(result["causal_length"])
+            self.assertIsNotNone(witness)
+            self.assertLessEqual(len(witness), result["state_bound"])
+            self.assertTrue(periodic_collision(digits, m, witness))

+def _collision_graph(
+    digits: tuple[int, ...], m: int
+) -> dict[tuple[int, ...], tuple[tuple[int, ...], ...]]:
+    """Build the bounded-difference collision graph at aperture ``m``."""
+    if m < 2:
+        raise ValueError("the collision graph requires m>=2")
+    d = digits[0]
+    q = q_sequence(digits, m)
+    modulus = q[m]
+    vertices = product(range(-d, d + 1), repeat=m - 1)
+    adjacency: dict[tuple[int, ...], tuple[tuple[int, ...], ...]] = {}
+    for vertex in vertices:
+        following = []
+        for appended in range(-d, d + 1):
+            weighted = sum(q[j] * vertex[j] for j in range(m - 1))
+            weighted += q[m - 1] * appended
+            if weighted % modulus == 0:
+                following.append(vertex[1:] + (appended,))
+        adjacency[vertex] = tuple(following)
+    return adjacency
+
+
+def _reachable_cycle(
+    adjacency: dict[tuple[int, ...], tuple[tuple[int, ...], ...]],
+    starts: list[tuple[int, ...]],
+) -> tuple[int, ...] | None:
+    """Return the first-coordinate word on a cycle reachable from ``starts``."""
+    color: dict[tuple[int, ...], int] = {}
+    parent: dict[tuple[int, ...], tuple[int, ...]] = {}
+
+    def visit(vertex: tuple[int, ...]) -> tuple[int, ...] | None:
+        color[vertex] = 1
+        for following in adjacency[vertex]:
+            if color.get(following, 0) == 0:
+                parent[following] = vertex
+                witness = visit(following)
+                if witness is not None:
+                    return witness
+            elif color[following] == 1:
+                reverse_cycle = [vertex]
+                while reverse_cycle[-1] != following:
+                    reverse_cycle.append(parent[reverse_cycle[-1]])
+                cycle = tuple(reversed(reverse_cycle))
+                return tuple(state[0] for state in cycle)
+        color[vertex] = 2
+        return None
+
+    for start in starts:
+        if color.get(start, 0) == 0:
+            witness = visit(start)
+            if witness is not None:
+                return witness
+    return None
+
+
+def collision_graph_analysis(
+    digits: tuple[int, ...], m: int
+) -> dict[str, int | bool | tuple[int, ...] | None]:
+    """Return the exact injectivity, causal-depth, and cycle certificates."""
+    adjacency = _collision_graph(digits, m)
+    zero = (0,) * (m - 1)
+    starts = [vertex for vertex in adjacency if vertex[0] != 0]
+    zero_predecessors = [vertex for vertex, targets in adjacency.items() if zero in targets]
+    periodic_witness = _reachable_cycle(adjacency, starts)
+    if periodic_witness is not None and periodic_witness[0] < 0:
+        periodic_witness = tuple(-entry for entry in periodic_witness)
+    injective = periodic_witness is None
+
+    causal_length = None
+    if injective:
+        longest_cache: dict[tuple[int, ...], int] = {}
+
+        def longest_path(vertex: tuple[int, ...]) -> int:
+            if vertex not in longest_cache:
+                longest_cache[vertex] = max(
+                    (1 + longest_path(target) for target in adjacency[vertex]),
+                    default=0,
+                )
+            return longest_cache[vertex]
+
+        causal_length = 1 + max(longest_path(start) for start in starts)
+
+    return {
+        "injective": injective,
+        "causal_length": causal_length,
+        "periodic_witness": periodic_witness,
+        "zero_predecessor_is_unique": zero_predecessors == [zero],
+        "state_bound": len(adjacency) - 1,
+    }
+
+
+def aperture_two_claims(
+    digits: tuple[int, ...],
+) -> dict[str, int | str | tuple[int, ...] | None]:
+    """Classify aperture two by the second-digit boundary parameter."""
+    if len(digits) < 2:
+        raise ValueError("the aperture-two classification requires Parry order p>=2")
+    d = digits[0]
+    boundary = digits[1] + (1 if len(digits) > 2 else 0)
+    analysis = collision_graph_analysis(digits, 2)
+    if boundary == d + 1:
+        regime = "local_bijection"
+    elif boundary == d:
+        regime = "constant_branch_pair"
+    else:
+        regime = "two_output_inverse"
+    return {
+        "boundary_parameter": boundary,
+        "regime": regime,
+        "causal_length": analysis["causal_length"],
+        "periodic_witness": analysis["periodic_witness"],
+    }

+\begin{corollary}[Causal completeness and periodic detection]
+\label{cor:simple-parry-causal-completeness}
+Under the preceding hypotheses, for every $m\ge2$ the following are
+equivalent:
+\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\roman*)}]
+  \item $\Phi_{\beta,m}$ is injective;
+  \item $\ell_{\rm cau}(\beta,m)<\infty$;
+  \item no directed cycle of $\Gamma_{\beta,m}$ is reachable from $B$.
+\end{enumerate}
+If these conditions hold, then
+\begin{equation}
+1\le \ell_{\rm cau}(\beta,m)
+\le (2d+1)^{m-1}-1.
+\label{eq:simple-parry-causal-state-bound}
+\end{equation}
+If they fail, there are distinct periodic raw points with the same image and
+with common period at most $(2d+1)^{m-1}-1$.  Thus injectivity in this class
+can be decided by a finite forward cycle search, and every failure has a
+bounded periodic certificate.
+\end{corollary}
+
+\begin{proof}
+The recurrence \eqref{eq:simple-parry-Q} gives $Q_1=d+1$ and shows
+inductively that $Q_n>Q_{n-1}$: before the terminal index there is the
+additional summand $1$, while at and after that index the positive term
+$t_pQ_{n-p}$ accompanies $dQ_{n-1}$.  In particular, $Q_m>d$.
+
+Let $\mathbf0=(0,\ldots,0)\in\Delta_d^{m-1}$.  If an edge
+$v\to\mathbf0$ exists, the overlap conditions give
+$v_1=\cdots=v_{m-2}=0$, and the edge congruence reduces to
+$v_0\equiv0\pmod{Q_m}$.  Since $|v_0|\le d<Q_m$, necessarily
+$v=\mathbf0$.  Hence the zero vertex has the zero vertex as its unique
+predecessor and is not reachable from $B$.
+
+If $\Phi_{\beta,m}$ is injective, the last assertion of
+Theorem~\ref{thm:simple-parry-causal-collision} now gives a finite causal
+inverse.  The converse is immediate because a decoder recovers every raw
+coordinate.  A directed cycle reachable from $B$ cannot contain
+$\mathbf0$; repeating its first-coordinate labels gives a nonzero periodic
+difference sequence and hence, by taking positive and negative parts, two
+distinct periodic raw points with the same image.  Conversely, from any
+nonzero bi-infinite collision path, shift to a vertex in $B$.  Its forward
+path avoids $\mathbf0$ and therefore repeats among the
+$(2d+1)^{m-1}-1$ nonzero vertices, producing a reachable directed cycle.
+This proves all three equivalences and the periodic certificate, whose cycle
+may be chosen simple.
+
+In the injective case the forward subgraph reachable from $B$ is acyclic and
+contains at most $(2d+1)^{m-1}-1$ vertices.  A directed path in it has at
+most $(2d+1)^{m-1}-2$ edges.  Formula
+\eqref{eq:collision-graph-longest-path} then gives
+\eqref{eq:simple-parry-causal-state-bound}.
+\end{proof}
+
+\begin{theorem}[Complete aperture-two trichotomy]
+\label{thm:simple-parry-aperture-two}
+Set
+\[
+c_\beta=t_2+\ind_{\{p\ge3\}}.
+\]
+Then $1\le c_\beta\le d+1$ and
+\[
+Q_2=d(d+1)+c_\beta.
+\]
+Exactly one of the following alternatives holds.
+\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\alph*)}]
+  \item If $c_\beta=d+1$, then $\Fold_{\beta,2}$ is the identity on
+  $\mathcal A_d^2$ and $\ell_{\rm cau}(\beta,2)=1$.
+  \item If $1\le c_\beta<d$, then $\Phi_{\beta,2}$ is injective and
+  $\ell_{\rm cau}(\beta,2)=2$.
+  \item If $c_\beta=d$, then $\Phi_{\beta,2}$ is noninjective.  Its sole
+  nonsingleton path-space fiber is
+  \[
+  \Phi_{\beta,2}(0^{\mathbb Z})
+  =\Phi_{\beta,2}(d^{\mathbb Z})
+  =((0,0))^{\mathbb Z},
+  \]
+  and $\ell_{\rm cau}(\beta,2)=\infty$.
+\end{enumerate}
+For $p=2$ the three cases are determined by $c_\beta=t_2$; for
+$p\ge3$ they are determined by $c_\beta=t_2+1$.  In particular, a binary
+simple-Parry word of order at least three has an identity aperture-two fold
+when $t_2=1$ and exactly the displayed constant branch pair when $t_2=0$.
+\end{theorem}
+
+\begin{proof}
+Put $q=d+1$ and $M=Q_2=dq+c_\beta$.  The formula for $Q_2$ follows directly
+from \eqref{eq:simple-parry-Q}, with the boundary summand $1$ present exactly
+when $2<p$.  Since $t_2\ge1$ when $p=2$, whereas $0\le t_2\le d$ when
+$p\ge3$, the stated range for $c_\beta$ follows.
+
+An edge of $\Gamma_{\beta,2}$ is a pair $(e,f)\in\Delta_d^2$ satisfying
+\begin{equation}
+e+qf\equiv0\pmod M.
+\label{eq:aperture-two-edge-congruence}
+\end{equation}
+The left side has modulus at most
+$d(1+q)=q^2-1<2M$, so it equals $-M$, $0$, or $M$.  If it is zero, then
+$q>|e|$ forces $(e,f)=(0,0)$.  If it is $M$, the bound $e\le d$ forces
+$f=d$, because $f\le d-1$ would give
+$M-qf\ge q+c_\beta>d$; hence $(e,f)=(c_\beta,d)$, which is admissible
+exactly when $c_\beta\le d$.  The case $-M$ is its negative.  Thus the full
+edge set is
+\[
+\{(0,0)\}\quad(c_\beta=d+1),
+\qquad
+\{(0,0),\ \pm(c_\beta,d)\}\quad(c_\beta\le d).
+\]
+
+When $c_\beta=d+1$, one has $Q_2=q^2=|\mathcal A_d^2|$, so every raw
+length-two word is legal and cyclic reduction does nothing.  This proves
+(a).  If $c_\beta<d$, the two nonzero edges cannot be followed by another
+edge, because their terminal vertices are $\pm d$, not $\pm c_\beta$.
+There is a one-output collision but no two-output collision, so
+Theorem~\ref{thm:simple-parry-causal-collision} gives (b).  Finally, when
+$c_\beta=d$, the two nonzero edges are the loops $(d,d)$ and $(-d,-d)$.
+They give precisely the constant difference sequences $\pm d^{\mathbb Z}$.
+The only raw realization of either is the pair
+$\{0^{\mathbb Z},d^{\mathbb Z}\}$, and the common residue is zero in every
+window.  No other nonzero bi-infinite path exists, proving (c) and the fiber
+classification.
+\end{proof}
+

+\begin{corollary}[Causal completeness and periodic detection]
+\label{cor:simple-parry-causal-completeness}
+Under the preceding hypotheses, for every $m\ge2$ the following are
+equivalent:
+\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\roman*)}]
+  \item $\Phi_{\beta,m}$ is injective;
+  \item $\ell_{\rm cau}(\beta,m)<\infty$;
+  \item no directed cycle of $\Gamma_{\beta,m}$ is reachable from $B$.
+\end{enumerate}
+If these conditions hold, then
+\begin{equation}
+1\le \ell_{\rm cau}(\beta,m)
+\le (2d+1)^{m-1}-1.
+\label{eq:simple-parry-causal-state-bound}
+\end{equation}
+If they fail, there are distinct periodic raw points with the same image and
+with common period at most $(2d+1)^{m-1}-1$.  Thus injectivity in this class
+can be decided by a finite forward cycle search, and every failure has a
+bounded periodic certificate.
+\end{corollary}
+
+\begin{proof}
+The recurrence \eqref{eq:simple-parry-Q} gives $Q_1=d+1$ and shows
+inductively that $Q_n>Q_{n-1}$: before the terminal index there is the
+additional summand $1$, while at and after that index the positive term
+$t_pQ_{n-p}$ accompanies $dQ_{n-1}$.  In particular, $Q_m>d$.
+
+Let $\mathbf0=(0,\ldots,0)\in\Delta_d^{m-1}$.  If an edge
+$v\to\mathbf0$ exists, the overlap conditions give
+$v_1=\cdots=v_{m-2}=0$, and the edge congruence reduces to
+$v_0\equiv0\pmod{Q_m}$.  Since $|v_0|\le d<Q_m$, necessarily
+$v=\mathbf0$.  Hence the zero vertex has the zero vertex as its unique
+predecessor and is not reachable from $B$.
+
+If $\Phi_{\beta,m}$ is injective, the last assertion of
+Theorem~\ref{thm:simple-parry-causal-collision} now gives a finite causal
+inverse.  The converse is immediate because a decoder recovers every raw
+coordinate.  A directed cycle reachable from $B$ cannot contain
+$\mathbf0$; repeating its first-coordinate labels gives a nonzero periodic
+difference sequence and hence, by taking positive and negative parts, two
+distinct periodic raw points with the same image.  Conversely, from any
+nonzero bi-infinite collision path, shift to a vertex in $B$.  Its forward
+path avoids $\mathbf0$ and therefore repeats among the
+$(2d+1)^{m-1}-1$ nonzero vertices, producing a reachable directed cycle.
+This proves all three equivalences and the periodic certificate, whose cycle
+may be chosen simple.
+
+In the injective case the forward subgraph reachable from $B$ is acyclic and
+contains at most $(2d+1)^{m-1}-1$ vertices.  A directed path in it has at
+most $(2d+1)^{m-1}-2$ edges.  Formula
+\eqref{eq:collision-graph-longest-path} then gives
+\eqref{eq:simple-parry-causal-state-bound}.
+\end{proof}
+
+\begin{theorem}[Complete aperture-two trichotomy]
+\label{thm:simple-parry-aperture-two}
+Set
+\[
+c_\beta=t_2+\ind_{\{p\ge3\}}.
+\]
+Then $1\le c_\beta\le d+1$ and
+\[
+Q_2=d(d+1)+c_\beta.
+\]
+Exactly one of the following alternatives holds.
+\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\alph*)}]
+  \item If $c_\beta=d+1$, then $\Fold_{\beta,2}$ is the identity on
+  $\mathcal A_d^2$ and $\ell_{\rm cau}(\beta,2)=1$.
+  \item If $1\le c_\beta<d$, then $\Phi_{\beta,2}$ is injective and
+  $\ell_{\rm cau}(\beta,2)=2$.
+  \item If $c_\beta=d$, then $\Phi_{\beta,2}$ is noninjective.  Its sole
+  nonsingleton path-space fiber is
+  \[
+  \Phi_{\beta,2}(0^{\mathbb Z})
+  =\Phi_{\beta,2}(d^{\mathbb Z})
+  =((0,0))^{\mathbb Z},
+  \]
+  and $\ell_{\rm cau}(\beta,2)=\infty$.
+\end{enumerate}
+For $p=2$ the three cases are determined by $c_\beta=t_2$; for
+$p\ge3$ they are determined by $c_\beta=t_2+1$.  In particular, a binary
+simple-Parry word of order at least three has an identity aperture-two fold
+when $t_2=1$ and exactly the displayed constant branch pair when $t_2=0$.
+\end{theorem}
+
+\begin{proof}
+Put $q=d+1$ and $M=Q_2=dq+c_\beta$.  The formula for $Q_2$ follows directly
+from \eqref{eq:simple-parry-Q}, with the boundary summand $1$ present exactly
+when $2<p$.  Since $t_2\ge1$ when $p=2$, whereas $0\le t_2\le d$ when
+$p\ge3$, the stated range for $c_\beta$ follows.
+
+An edge of $\Gamma_{\beta,2}$ is a pair $(e,f)\in\Delta_d^2$ satisfying
+\begin{equation}
+e+qf\equiv0\pmod M.
+\label{eq:aperture-two-edge-congruence}
+\end{equation}
+The left side has modulus at most
+$d(1+q)=q^2-1<2M$, so it equals $-M$, $0$, or $M$.  If it is zero, then
+$q>|e|$ forces $(e,f)=(0,0)$.  If it is $M$, the bound $e\le d$ forces
+$f=d$, because $f\le d-1$ would give
+$M-qf\ge q+c_\beta>d$; hence $(e,f)=(c_\beta,d)$, which is admissible
+exactly when $c_\beta\le d$.  The case $-M$ is its negative.  Thus the full
+edge set is
+\[
+\{(0,0)\}\quad(c_\beta=d+1),
+\qquad
+\{(0,0),\ \pm(c_\beta,d)\}\quad(c_\beta\le d).
+\]
+
+When $c_\beta=d+1$, one has $Q_2=q^2=|\mathcal A_d^2|$, so every raw
+length-two word is legal and cyclic reduction does nothing.  This proves
+(a).  If $c_\beta<d$, the two nonzero edges cannot be followed by another
+edge, because their terminal vertices are $\pm d$, not $\pm c_\beta$.
+There is a one-output collision but no two-output collision, so
+Theorem~\ref{thm:simple-parry-causal-collision} gives (b).  Finally, when
+$c_\beta=d$, the two nonzero edges are the loops $(d,d)$ and $(-d,-d)$.
+They give precisely the constant difference sequences $\pm d^{\mathbb Z}$.
+The only raw realization of either is the pair
+$\{0^{\mathbb Z},d^{\mathbb Z}\}$, and the common residue is zero in every
+window.  No other nonzero bi-infinite path exists, proving (c) and the fiber
+classification.
+\end{proof}
+
 The graph in Theorem~\ref{thm:simple-parry-causal-collision} is the arithmetic
 specialization of the standard fiber-product collision graph for a sliding
 block code; see \cite{LindMarcus1995,Nasu1995}.  Its substantive role here is

+def _collision_graph(
+    digits: tuple[int, ...], m: int
+) -> dict[tuple[int, ...], tuple[tuple[int, ...], ...]]:
+    """Build the bounded-difference collision graph at aperture ``m``."""
+    if m < 2:
+        raise ValueError("the collision graph requires m>=2")
+    d = digits[0]
+    q = q_sequence(digits, m)
+    modulus = q[m]
+    vertices = product(range(-d, d + 1), repeat=m - 1)
+    adjacency: dict[tuple[int, ...], tuple[tuple[int, ...], ...]] = {}
+    for vertex in vertices:
+        following = []
+        for appended in range(-d, d + 1):
+            weighted = sum(q[j] * vertex[j] for j in range(m - 1))
+            weighted += q[m - 1] * appended
+            if weighted % modulus == 0:
+                following.append(vertex[1:] + (appended,))
+        adjacency[vertex] = tuple(following)
+    return adjacency
+
+
+def _reachable_cycle(
+    adjacency: dict[tuple[int, ...], tuple[tuple[int, ...], ...]],
+    starts: list[tuple[int, ...]],
+) -> tuple[int, ...] | None:
+    """Return the first-coordinate word on a cycle reachable from ``starts``."""
+    color: dict[tuple[int, ...], int] = {}
+    parent: dict[tuple[int, ...], tuple[int, ...]] = {}
+
+    def visit(vertex: tuple[int, ...]) -> tuple[int, ...] | None:
+        color[vertex] = 1
+        for following in adjacency[vertex]:
+            if color.get(following, 0) == 0:
+                parent[following] = vertex
+                witness = visit(following)
+                if witness is not None:
+                    return witness
+            elif color[following] == 1:
+                reverse_cycle = [vertex]
+                while reverse_cycle[-1] != following:
+                    reverse_cycle.append(parent[reverse_cycle[-1]])
+                cycle = tuple(reversed(reverse_cycle))
+                return tuple(state[0] for state in cycle)
+        color[vertex] = 2
+        return None
+
+    for start in starts:
+        if color.get(start, 0) == 0:
+            witness = visit(start)
+            if witness is not None:
+                return witness
+    return None
+
+
+def collision_graph_analysis(
+    digits: tuple[int, ...], m: int
+) -> dict[str, int | bool | tuple[int, ...] | None]:
+    """Return the exact injectivity, causal-depth, and cycle certificates."""
+    adjacency = _collision_graph(digits, m)
+    zero = (0,) * (m - 1)
+    starts = [vertex for vertex in adjacency if vertex[0] != 0]
+    zero_predecessors = [vertex for vertex, targets in adjacency.items() if zero in targets]
+    periodic_witness = _reachable_cycle(adjacency, starts)
+    if periodic_witness is not None and periodic_witness[0] < 0:
+        periodic_witness = tuple(-entry for entry in periodic_witness)
+    injective = periodic_witness is None
+
+    causal_length = None
+    if injective:
+        longest_cache: dict[tuple[int, ...], int] = {}
+
+        def longest_path(vertex: tuple[int, ...]) -> int:
+            if vertex not in longest_cache:
+                longest_cache[vertex] = max(
+                    (1 + longest_path(target) for target in adjacency[vertex]),
+                    default=0,
+                )
+            return longest_cache[vertex]
+
+        causal_length = 1 + max(longest_path(start) for start in starts)
+
+    return {
+        "injective": injective,
+        "causal_length": causal_length,
+        "periodic_witness": periodic_witness,
+        "zero_predecessor_is_unique": zero_predecessors == [zero],
+        "state_bound": len(adjacency) - 1,
+    }
+
+
+def aperture_two_claims(
+    digits: tuple[int, ...],
+) -> dict[str, int | str | tuple[int, ...] | None]:
+    """Classify aperture two by the second-digit boundary parameter."""
+    if len(digits) < 2:
+        raise ValueError("the aperture-two classification requires Parry order p>=2")
+    d = digits[0]
+    boundary = digits[1] + (1 if len(digits) > 2 else 0)
+    analysis = collision_graph_analysis(digits, 2)
+    if boundary == d + 1:
+        regime = "local_bijection"
+    elif boundary == d:
+        regime = "constant_branch_pair"
+    else:
+        regime = "two_output_inverse"
+    return {
+        "boundary_parameter": boundary,
+        "regime": regime,
+        "causal_length": analysis["causal_length"],
+        "periodic_witness": analysis["periodic_witness"],
+    }
+

+def _collision_graph(
+    digits: tuple[int, ...], m: int
+) -> dict[tuple[int, ...], tuple[tuple[int, ...], ...]]:
+    """Build the bounded-difference collision graph at aperture ``m``."""
+    if m < 2:
+        raise ValueError("the collision graph requires m>=2")
+    d = digits[0]
+    q = q_sequence(digits, m)
+    modulus = q[m]
+    vertices = product(range(-d, d + 1), repeat=m - 1)
+    adjacency: dict[tuple[int, ...], tuple[tuple[int, ...], ...]] = {}
+    for vertex in vertices:
+        following = []
+        for appended in range(-d, d + 1):
+            weighted = sum(q[j] * vertex[j] for j in range(m - 1))
+            weighted += q[m - 1] * appended
+            if weighted % modulus == 0:
+                following.append(vertex[1:] + (appended,))
+        adjacency[vertex] = tuple(following)
+    return adjacency
+
+
+def _reachable_cycle(
+    adjacency: dict[tuple[int, ...], tuple[tuple[int, ...], ...]],
+    starts: list[tuple[int, ...]],
+) -> tuple[int, ...] | None:
+    """Return the first-coordinate word on a cycle reachable from ``starts``."""
+    color: dict[tuple[int, ...], int] = {}
+    parent: dict[tuple[int, ...], tuple[int, ...]] = {}
+
+    def visit(vertex: tuple[int, ...]) -> tuple[int, ...] | None:
+        color[vertex] = 1
+        for following in adjacency[vertex]:
+            if color.get(following, 0) == 0:
+                parent[following] = vertex
+                witness = visit(following)
+                if witness is not None:
+                    return witness
+            elif color[following] == 1:
+                reverse_cycle = [vertex]
+                while reverse_cycle[-1] != following:
+                    reverse_cycle.append(parent[reverse_cycle[-1]])
+                cycle = tuple(reversed(reverse_cycle))
+                return tuple(state[0] for state in cycle)
+        color[vertex] = 2
+        return None
+
+    for start in starts:
+        if color.get(start, 0) == 0:
+            witness = visit(start)
+            if witness is not None:
+                return witness
+    return None
+
+
+def collision_graph_analysis(
+    digits: tuple[int, ...], m: int
+) -> dict[str, int | bool | tuple[int, ...] | None]:
+    """Return the exact injectivity, causal-depth, and cycle certificates."""
+    adjacency = _collision_graph(digits, m)
+    zero = (0,) * (m - 1)
+    starts = [vertex for vertex in adjacency if vertex[0] != 0]
+    zero_predecessors = [vertex for vertex, targets in adjacency.items() if zero in targets]
+    periodic_witness = _reachable_cycle(adjacency, starts)
+    if periodic_witness is not None and periodic_witness[0] < 0:
+        periodic_witness = tuple(-entry for entry in periodic_witness)
+    injective = periodic_witness is None
+
+    causal_length = None
+    if injective:
+        longest_cache: dict[tuple[int, ...], int] = {}
+
+        def longest_path(vertex: tuple[int, ...]) -> int:
+            if vertex not in longest_cache:
+                longest_cache[vertex] = max(
+                    (1 + longest_path(target) for target in adjacency[vertex]),
+                    default=0,
+                )
+            return longest_cache[vertex]
+
+        causal_length = 1 + max(longest_path(start) for start in starts)
+
+    return {
+        "injective": injective,
+        "causal_length": causal_length,
+        "periodic_witness": periodic_witness,
+        "zero_predecessor_is_unique": zero_predecessors == [zero],
+        "state_bound": len(adjacency) - 1,
+    }
+
+
+def aperture_two_claims(
+    digits: tuple[int, ...],
+) -> dict[str, int | str | tuple[int, ...] | None]:
+    """Classify aperture two by the second-digit boundary parameter."""
+    if len(digits) < 2:
+        raise ValueError("the aperture-two classification requires Parry order p>=2")
+    d = digits[0]
+    boundary = digits[1] + (1 if len(digits) > 2 else 0)
+    analysis = collision_graph_analysis(digits, 2)
+    if boundary == d + 1:
+        regime = "local_bijection"
+    elif boundary == d:
+        regime = "constant_branch_pair"
+    else:
+        regime = "two_output_inverse"
+    return {
+        "boundary_parameter": boundary,
+        "regime": regime,
+        "causal_length": analysis["causal_length"],
+        "periodic_witness": analysis["periodic_witness"],
+    }

+\begin{corollary}[Causal completeness and periodic detection]
+\label{cor:simple-parry-causal-completeness}
+Under the preceding hypotheses, for every $m\ge2$ the following are
+equivalent:
+\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\roman*)}]
+  \item $\Phi_{\beta,m}$ is injective;
+  \item $\ell_{\rm cau}(\beta,m)<\infty$;
+  \item no directed cycle of $\Gamma_{\beta,m}$ is reachable from $B$.
+\end{enumerate}
+If these conditions hold, then
+\begin{equation}
+1\le \ell_{\rm cau}(\beta,m)
+\le (2d+1)^{m-1}-1.
+\label{eq:simple-parry-causal-state-bound}
+\end{equation}
+If they fail, there are distinct periodic raw points with the same image and
+with common period at most $(2d+1)^{m-1}-1$.  Thus injectivity in this class
+can be decided by a finite forward cycle search, and every failure has a
+bounded periodic certificate.
+\end{corollary}
+
+\begin{proof}
+The recurrence \eqref{eq:simple-parry-Q} gives $Q_1=d+1$ and shows
+inductively that $Q_n>Q_{n-1}$: before the terminal index there is the
+additional summand $1$, while at and after that index the positive term
+$t_pQ_{n-p}$ accompanies $dQ_{n-1}$.  In particular, $Q_m>d$.
+
+Let $\mathbf0=(0,\ldots,0)\in\Delta_d^{m-1}$.  If an edge
+$v\to\mathbf0$ exists, the overlap conditions give
+$v_1=\cdots=v_{m-2}=0$, and the edge congruence reduces to
+$v_0\equiv0\pmod{Q_m}$.  Since $|v_0|\le d<Q_m$, necessarily
+$v=\mathbf0$.  Hence the zero vertex has the zero vertex as its unique
+predecessor and is not reachable from $B$.
+
+If $\Phi_{\beta,m}$ is injective, the last assertion of
+Theorem~\ref{thm:simple-parry-causal-collision} now gives a finite causal
+inverse.  The converse is immediate because a decoder recovers every raw
+coordinate.  A directed cycle reachable from $B$ cannot contain
+$\mathbf0$; repeating its first-coordinate labels gives a nonzero periodic
+difference sequence and hence, by taking positive and negative parts, two
+distinct periodic raw points with the same image.  Conversely, from any
+nonzero bi-infinite collision path, shift to a vertex in $B$.  Its forward
+path avoids $\mathbf0$ and therefore repeats among the
+$(2d+1)^{m-1}-1$ nonzero vertices, producing a reachable directed cycle.
+This proves all three equivalences and the periodic certificate, whose cycle
+may be chosen simple.
+
+In the injective case the forward subgraph reachable from $B$ is acyclic and
+contains at most $(2d+1)^{m-1}-1$ vertices.  A directed path in it has at
+most $(2d+1)^{m-1}-2$ edges.  Formula
+\eqref{eq:collision-graph-longest-path} then gives
+\eqref{eq:simple-parry-causal-state-bound}.
+\end{proof}
+
+\begin{theorem}[Complete aperture-two trichotomy]
+\label{thm:simple-parry-aperture-two}
+Set
+\[
+c_\beta=t_2+\ind_{\{p\ge3\}}.
+\]
+Then $1\le c_\beta\le d+1$ and
+\[
+Q_2=d(d+1)+c_\beta.
+\]
+Exactly one of the following alternatives holds.
+\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\alph*)}]
+  \item If $c_\beta=d+1$, then $\Fold_{\beta,2}$ is the identity on
+  $\mathcal A_d^2$ and $\ell_{\rm cau}(\beta,2)=1$.
+  \item If $1\le c_\beta<d$, then $\Phi_{\beta,2}$ is injective and
+  $\ell_{\rm cau}(\beta,2)=2$.
+  \item If $c_\beta=d$, then $\Phi_{\beta,2}$ is noninjective.  Its sole
+  nonsingleton path-space fiber is
+  \[
+  \Phi_{\beta,2}(0^{\mathbb Z})
+  =\Phi_{\beta,2}(d^{\mathbb Z})
+  =((0,0))^{\mathbb Z},
+  \]
+  and $\ell_{\rm cau}(\beta,2)=\infty$.
+\end{enumerate}
+For $p=2$ the three cases are determined by $c_\beta=t_2$; for
+$p\ge3$ they are determined by $c_\beta=t_2+1$.  In particular, a binary
+simple-Parry word of order at least three has an identity aperture-two fold
+when $t_2=1$ and exactly the displayed constant branch pair when $t_2=0$.
+\end{theorem}
+
+\begin{proof}
+Put $q=d+1$ and $M=Q_2=dq+c_\beta$.  The formula for $Q_2$ follows directly
+from \eqref{eq:simple-parry-Q}, with the boundary summand $1$ present exactly
+when $2<p$.  Since $t_2\ge1$ when $p=2$, whereas $0\le t_2\le d$ when
+$p\ge3$, the stated range for $c_\beta$ follows.
+
+An edge of $\Gamma_{\beta,2}$ is a pair $(e,f)\in\Delta_d^2$ satisfying
+\begin{equation}
+e+qf\equiv0\pmod M.
+\label{eq:aperture-two-edge-congruence}
+\end{equation}
+The left side has modulus at most
+$d(1+q)=q^2-1<2M$, so it equals $-M$, $0$, or $M$.  If it is zero, then
+$q>|e|$ forces $(e,f)=(0,0)$.  If it is $M$, the bound $e\le d$ forces
+$f=d$, because $f\le d-1$ would give
+$M-qf\ge q+c_\beta>d$; hence $(e,f)=(c_\beta,d)$, which is admissible
+exactly when $c_\beta\le d$.  The case $-M$ is its negative.  Thus the full
+edge set is
+\[
+\{(0,0)\}\quad(c_\beta=d+1),
+\qquad
+\{(0,0),\ \pm(c_\beta,d)\}\quad(c_\beta\le d).
+\]
+
+When $c_\beta=d+1$, one has $Q_2=q^2=|\mathcal A_d^2|$, so every raw
+length-two word is legal and cyclic reduction does nothing.  This proves
+(a).  If $c_\beta<d$, the two nonzero edges cannot be followed by another
+edge, because their terminal vertices are $\pm d$, not $\pm c_\beta$.
+There is a one-output collision but no two-output collision, so
+Theorem~\ref{thm:simple-parry-causal-collision} gives (b).  Finally, when
+$c_\beta=d$, the two nonzero edges are the loops $(d,d)$ and $(-d,-d)$.
+They give precisely the constant difference sequences $\pm d^{\mathbb Z}$.
+The only raw realization of either is the pair
+$\{0^{\mathbb Z},d^{\mathbb Z}\}$, and the common residue is zero in every
+window.  No other nonzero bi-infinite path exists, proving (c) and the fiber
+classification.
+\end{proof}
+

+def _collision_graph(
+    digits: tuple[int, ...], m: int
+) -> dict[tuple[int, ...], tuple[tuple[int, ...], ...]]:
+    """Build the bounded-difference collision graph at aperture ``m``."""
+    if m < 2:
+        raise ValueError("the collision graph requires m>=2")
+    d = digits[0]
+    q = q_sequence(digits, m)
+    modulus = q[m]
+    vertices = product(range(-d, d + 1), repeat=m - 1)
+    adjacency: dict[tuple[int, ...], tuple[tuple[int, ...], ...]] = {}
+    for vertex in vertices:
+        following = []
+        for appended in range(-d, d + 1):
+            weighted = sum(q[j] * vertex[j] for j in range(m - 1))
+            weighted += q[m - 1] * appended
+            if weighted % modulus == 0:
+                following.append(vertex[1:] + (appended,))
+        adjacency[vertex] = tuple(following)
+    return adjacency
+
+
+def _reachable_cycle(
+    adjacency: dict[tuple[int, ...], tuple[tuple[int, ...], ...]],
+    starts: list[tuple[int, ...]],
+) -> tuple[int, ...] | None:
+    """Return the first-coordinate word on a cycle reachable from ``starts``."""
+    color: dict[tuple[int, ...], int] = {}
+    parent: dict[tuple[int, ...], tuple[int, ...]] = {}
+
+    def visit(vertex: tuple[int, ...]) -> tuple[int, ...] | None:
+        color[vertex] = 1
+        for following in adjacency[vertex]:
+            if color.get(following, 0) == 0:
+                parent[following] = vertex
+                witness = visit(following)
+                if witness is not None:
+                    return witness
+            elif color[following] == 1:
+                reverse_cycle = [vertex]
+                while reverse_cycle[-1] != following:
+                    reverse_cycle.append(parent[reverse_cycle[-1]])
+                cycle = tuple(reversed(reverse_cycle))
+                return tuple(state[0] for state in cycle)
+        color[vertex] = 2
+        return None
+
+    for start in starts:
+        if color.get(start, 0) == 0:
+            witness = visit(start)
+            if witness is not None:
+                return witness
+    return None
+
+
+def collision_graph_analysis(
+    digits: tuple[int, ...], m: int
+) -> dict[str, int | bool | tuple[int, ...] | None]:
+    """Return the exact injectivity, causal-depth, and cycle certificates."""
+    adjacency = _collision_graph(digits, m)
+    zero = (0,) * (m - 1)
+    starts = [vertex for vertex in adjacency if vertex[0] != 0]
+    zero_predecessors = [vertex for vertex, targets in adjacency.items() if zero in targets]
+    periodic_witness = _reachable_cycle(adjacency, starts)
+    if periodic_witness is not None and periodic_witness[0] < 0:
+        periodic_witness = tuple(-entry for entry in periodic_witness)
+    injective = periodic_witness is None
+
+    causal_length = None
+    if injective:
+        longest_cache: dict[tuple[int, ...], int] = {}
+
+        def longest_path(vertex: tuple[int, ...]) -> int:
+            if vertex not in longest_cache:
+                longest_cache[vertex] = max(
+                    (1 + longest_path(target) for target in adjacency[vertex]),
+                    default=0,
+                )
+            return longest_cache[vertex]
+
+        causal_length = 1 + max(longest_path(start) for start in starts)
+
+    return {
+        "injective": injective,
+        "causal_length": causal_length,
+        "periodic_witness": periodic_witness,
+        "zero_predecessor_is_unique": zero_predecessors == [zero],
+        "state_bound": len(adjacency) - 1,
+    }
+
+
+def aperture_two_claims(
+    digits: tuple[int, ...],
+) -> dict[str, int | str | tuple[int, ...] | None]:
+    """Classify aperture two by the second-digit boundary parameter."""
+    if len(digits) < 2:
+        raise ValueError("the aperture-two classification requires Parry order p>=2")
+    d = digits[0]
+    boundary = digits[1] + (1 if len(digits) > 2 else 0)
+    analysis = collision_graph_analysis(digits, 2)
+    if boundary == d + 1:
+        regime = "local_bijection"
+    elif boundary == d:
+        regime = "constant_branch_pair"
+    else:
+        regime = "two_output_inverse"
+    return {
+        "boundary_parameter": boundary,
+        "regime": regime,
+        "causal_length": analysis["causal_length"],
+        "periodic_witness": analysis["periodic_witness"],
+    }
+

+\begin{corollary}[Causal completeness and periodic detection]
+\label{cor:simple-parry-causal-completeness}
+Under the preceding hypotheses, for every $m\ge2$ the following are
+equivalent:
+\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\roman*)}]
+  \item $\Phi_{\beta,m}$ is injective;
+  \item $\ell_{\rm cau}(\beta,m)<\infty$;
+  \item no directed cycle of $\Gamma_{\beta,m}$ is reachable from $B$.
+\end{enumerate}
+If these conditions hold, then
+\begin{equation}
+1\le \ell_{\rm cau}(\beta,m)
+\le (2d+1)^{m-1}-1.
+\label{eq:simple-parry-causal-state-bound}
+\end{equation}
+If they fail, there are distinct periodic raw points with the same image and
+with common period at most $(2d+1)^{m-1}-1$.  Thus injectivity in this class
+can be decided by a finite forward cycle search, and every failure has a
+bounded periodic certificate.
+\end{corollary}
+
+\begin{proof}
+The recurrence \eqref{eq:simple-parry-Q} gives $Q_1=d+1$ and shows
+inductively that $Q_n>Q_{n-1}$: before the terminal index there is the
+additional summand $1$, while at and after that index the positive term
+$t_pQ_{n-p}$ accompanies $dQ_{n-1}$.  In particular, $Q_m>d$.
+
+Let $\mathbf0=(0,\ldots,0)\in\Delta_d^{m-1}$.  If an edge
+$v\to\mathbf0$ exists, the overlap conditions give
+$v_1=\cdots=v_{m-2}=0$, and the edge congruence reduces to
+$v_0\equiv0\pmod{Q_m}$.  Since $|v_0|\le d<Q_m$, necessarily
+$v=\mathbf0$.  Hence the zero vertex has the zero vertex as its unique
+predecessor and is not reachable from $B$.
+
+If $\Phi_{\beta,m}$ is injective, the last assertion of
+Theorem~\ref{thm:simple-parry-causal-collision} now gives a finite causal
+inverse.  The converse is immediate because a decoder recovers every raw
+coordinate.  A directed cycle reachable from $B$ cannot contain
+$\mathbf0$; repeating its first-coordinate labels gives a nonzero periodic
+difference sequence and hence, by taking positive and negative parts, two
+distinct periodic raw points with the same image.  Conversely, from any
+nonzero bi-infinite collision path, shift to a vertex in $B$.  Its forward
+path avoids $\mathbf0$ and therefore repeats among the
+$(2d+1)^{m-1}-1$ nonzero vertices, producing a reachable directed cycle.
+This proves all three equivalences and the periodic certificate, whose cycle
+may be chosen simple.
+
+In the injective case the forward subgraph reachable from $B$ is acyclic and
+contains at most $(2d+1)^{m-1}-1$ vertices.  A directed path in it has at
+most $(2d+1)^{m-1}-2$ edges.  Formula
+\eqref{eq:collision-graph-longest-path} then gives
+\eqref{eq:simple-parry-causal-state-bound}.
+\end{proof}
+
+\begin{theorem}[Complete aperture-two trichotomy]
+\label{thm:simple-parry-aperture-two}
+Set
+\[
+c_\beta=t_2+\ind_{\{p\ge3\}}.
+\]
+Then $1\le c_\beta\le d+1$ and
+\[
+Q_2=d(d+1)+c_\beta.
+\]
+Exactly one of the following alternatives holds.
+\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\alph*)}]
+  \item If $c_\beta=d+1$, then $\Fold_{\beta,2}$ is the identity on
+  $\mathcal A_d^2$ and $\ell_{\rm cau}(\beta,2)=1$.
+  \item If $1\le c_\beta<d$, then $\Phi_{\beta,2}$ is injective and
+  $\ell_{\rm cau}(\beta,2)=2$.
+  \item If $c_\beta=d$, then $\Phi_{\beta,2}$ is noninjective.  Its sole
+  nonsingleton path-space fiber is
+  \[
+  \Phi_{\beta,2}(0^{\mathbb Z})
+  =\Phi_{\beta,2}(d^{\mathbb Z})
+  =((0,0))^{\mathbb Z},
+  \]
+  and $\ell_{\rm cau}(\beta,2)=\infty$.
+\end{enumerate}
+For $p=2$ the three cases are determined by $c_\beta=t_2$; for
+$p\ge3$ they are determined by $c_\beta=t_2+1$.  In particular, a binary
+simple-Parry word of order at least three has an identity aperture-two fold
+when $t_2=1$ and exactly the displayed constant branch pair when $t_2=0$.
+\end{theorem}
+
+\begin{proof}
+Put $q=d+1$ and $M=Q_2=dq+c_\beta$.  The formula for $Q_2$ follows directly
+from \eqref{eq:simple-parry-Q}, with the boundary summand $1$ present exactly
+when $2<p$.  Since $t_2\ge1$ when $p=2$, whereas $0\le t_2\le d$ when
+$p\ge3$, the stated range for $c_\beta$ follows.
+
+An edge of $\Gamma_{\beta,2}$ is a pair $(e,f)\in\Delta_d^2$ satisfying
+\begin{equation}
+e+qf\equiv0\pmod M.
+\label{eq:aperture-two-edge-congruence}
+\end{equation}
+The left side has modulus at most
+$d(1+q)=q^2-1<2M$, so it equals $-M$, $0$, or $M$.  If it is zero, then
+$q>|e|$ forces $(e,f)=(0,0)$.  If it is $M$, the bound $e\le d$ forces
+$f=d$, because $f\le d-1$ would give
+$M-qf\ge q+c_\beta>d$; hence $(e,f)=(c_\beta,d)$, which is admissible
+exactly when $c_\beta\le d$.  The case $-M$ is its negative.  Thus the full
+edge set is
+\[
+\{(0,0)\}\quad(c_\beta=d+1),
+\qquad
+\{(0,0),\ \pm(c_\beta,d)\}\quad(c_\beta\le d).
+\]
+
+When $c_\beta=d+1$, one has $Q_2=q^2=|\mathcal A_d^2|$, so every raw
+length-two word is legal and cyclic reduction does nothing.  This proves
+(a).  If $c_\beta<d$, the two nonzero edges cannot be followed by another
+edge, because their terminal vertices are $\pm d$, not $\pm c_\beta$.
+There is a one-output collision but no two-output collision, so
+Theorem~\ref{thm:simple-parry-causal-collision} gives (b).  Finally, when
+$c_\beta=d$, the two nonzero edges are the loops $(d,d)$ and $(-d,-d)$.
+They give precisely the constant difference sequences $\pm d^{\mathbb Z}$.
+The only raw realization of either is the pair
+$\{0^{\mathbb Z},d^{\mathbb Z}\}$, and the common residue is zero in every
+window.  No other nonzero bi-infinite path exists, proving (c) and the fiber
+classification.
+\end{proof}
+

 block code; see \cite{LindMarcus1995,Nasu1995}.  Its substantive role here is

+\ref{cor:simple-parry-causal-completeness} removes a possible intermediate
+regime: injectivity already forces a finite future-only inverse, with an
+explicit state-count bound, while noninjectivity always has a bounded
+periodic witness.  Theorem~\ref{thm:simple-parry-aperture-two} completely
+classifies aperture two and its only nontrivial branch locus from $t_2$.
+It remains open
 whether $\ell_{\rm cau}(\beta,m)$ is uniformly bounded over nonintegral cubic
 simple-Parry Pisot bases and their injective apertures.

+def _collision_graph(
+    digits: tuple[int, ...], m: int
+) -> dict[tuple[int, ...], tuple[tuple[int, ...], ...]]:
+    """Build the bounded-difference collision graph at aperture ``m``."""
+    if m < 2:
+        raise ValueError("the collision graph requires m>=2")
+    d = digits[0]
+    q = q_sequence(digits, m)
+    modulus = q[m]
+    vertices = product(range(-d, d + 1), repeat=m - 1)
+    adjacency: dict[tuple[int, ...], tuple[tuple[int, ...], ...]] = {}
+    for vertex in vertices:
+        following = []
+        for appended in range(-d, d + 1):
+            weighted = sum(q[j] * vertex[j] for j in range(m - 1))
+            weighted += q[m - 1] * appended
+            if weighted % modulus == 0:
+                following.append(vertex[1:] + (appended,))
+        adjacency[vertex] = tuple(following)
+    return adjacency
+
+
+def _reachable_cycle(
+    adjacency: dict[tuple[int, ...], tuple[tuple[int, ...], ...]],
+    starts: list[tuple[int, ...]],
+) -> tuple[int, ...] | None:
+    """Return the first-coordinate word on a cycle reachable from ``starts``."""
+    color: dict[tuple[int, ...], int] = {}
+    parent: dict[tuple[int, ...], tuple[int, ...]] = {}
+
+    def visit(vertex: tuple[int, ...]) -> tuple[int, ...] | None:
+        color[vertex] = 1
+        for following in adjacency[vertex]:
+            if color.get(following, 0) == 0:
+                parent[following] = vertex
+                witness = visit(following)
+                if witness is not None:
+                    return witness
+            elif color[following] == 1:
+                reverse_cycle = [vertex]
+                while reverse_cycle[-1] != following:
+                    reverse_cycle.append(parent[reverse_cycle[-1]])
+                cycle = tuple(reversed(reverse_cycle))
+                return tuple(state[0] for state in cycle)
+        color[vertex] = 2
+        return None
+
+    for start in starts:
+        if color.get(start, 0) == 0:
+            witness = visit(start)
+            if witness is not None:
+                return witness
+    return None
+
+
+def collision_graph_analysis(
+    digits: tuple[int, ...], m: int
+) -> dict[str, int | bool | tuple[int, ...] | None]:
+    """Return the exact injectivity, causal-depth, and cycle certificates."""
+    adjacency = _collision_graph(digits, m)
+    zero = (0,) * (m - 1)
+    starts = [vertex for vertex in adjacency if vertex[0] != 0]
+    zero_predecessors = [vertex for vertex, targets in adjacency.items() if zero in targets]
+    periodic_witness = _reachable_cycle(adjacency, starts)
+    if periodic_witness is not None and periodic_witness[0] < 0:
+        periodic_witness = tuple(-entry for entry in periodic_witness)
+    injective = periodic_witness is None
+
+    causal_length = None
+    if injective:
+        longest_cache: dict[tuple[int, ...], int] = {}
+
+        def longest_path(vertex: tuple[int, ...]) -> int:
+            if vertex not in longest_cache:
+                longest_cache[vertex] = max(
+                    (1 + longest_path(target) for target in adjacency[vertex]),
+                    default=0,
+                )
+            return longest_cache[vertex]
+
+        causal_length = 1 + max(longest_path(start) for start in starts)
+
+    return {
+        "injective": injective,
+        "causal_length": causal_length,
+        "periodic_witness": periodic_witness,
+        "zero_predecessor_is_unique": zero_predecessors == [zero],
+        "state_bound": len(adjacency) - 1,
+    }
+
+
+def aperture_two_claims(
+    digits: tuple[int, ...],
+) -> dict[str, int | str | tuple[int, ...] | None]:
+    """Classify aperture two by the second-digit boundary parameter."""
+    if len(digits) < 2:
+        raise ValueError("the aperture-two classification requires Parry order p>=2")
+    d = digits[0]
+    boundary = digits[1] + (1 if len(digits) > 2 else 0)
+    analysis = collision_graph_analysis(digits, 2)
+    if boundary == d + 1:
+        regime = "local_bijection"
+    elif boundary == d:
+        regime = "constant_branch_pair"
+    else:
+        regime = "two_output_inverse"
+    return {
+        "boundary_parameter": boundary,
+        "regime": regime,
+        "causal_length": analysis["causal_length"],
+        "periodic_witness": analysis["periodic_witness"],
+    }
+

+\begin{corollary}[Causal completeness and periodic detection]
+\label{cor:simple-parry-causal-completeness}
+Under the preceding hypotheses, for every $m\ge2$ the following are
+equivalent:
+\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\roman*)}]
+  \item $\Phi_{\beta,m}$ is injective;
+  \item $\ell_{\rm cau}(\beta,m)<\infty$;
+  \item no directed cycle of $\Gamma_{\beta,m}$ is reachable from $B$.
+\end{enumerate}
+If these conditions hold, then
+\begin{equation}
+1\le \ell_{\rm cau}(\beta,m)
+\le (2d+1)^{m-1}-1.
+\label{eq:simple-parry-causal-state-bound}
+\end{equation}
+If they fail, there are distinct periodic raw points with the same image and
+with common period at most $(2d+1)^{m-1}-1$.  Thus injectivity in this class
+can be decided by a finite forward cycle search, and every failure has a
+bounded periodic certificate.
+\end{corollary}
+
+\begin{proof}
+The recurrence \eqref{eq:simple-parry-Q} gives $Q_1=d+1$ and shows
+inductively that $Q_n>Q_{n-1}$: before the terminal index there is the
+additional summand $1$, while at and after that index the positive term
+$t_pQ_{n-p}$ accompanies $dQ_{n-1}$.  In particular, $Q_m>d$.
+
+Let $\mathbf0=(0,\ldots,0)\in\Delta_d^{m-1}$.  If an edge
+$v\to\mathbf0$ exists, the overlap conditions give
+$v_1=\cdots=v_{m-2}=0$, and the edge congruence reduces to
+$v_0\equiv0\pmod{Q_m}$.  Since $|v_0|\le d<Q_m$, necessarily
+$v=\mathbf0$.  Hence the zero vertex has the zero vertex as its unique
+predecessor and is not reachable from $B$.
+
+If $\Phi_{\beta,m}$ is injective, the last assertion of
+Theorem~\ref{thm:simple-parry-causal-collision} now gives a finite causal
+inverse.  The converse is immediate because a decoder recovers every raw
+coordinate.  A directed cycle reachable from $B$ cannot contain
+$\mathbf0$; repeating its first-coordinate labels gives a nonzero periodic
+difference sequence and hence, by taking positive and negative parts, two
+distinct periodic raw points with the same image.  Conversely, from any
+nonzero bi-infinite collision path, shift to a vertex in $B$.  Its forward
+path avoids $\mathbf0$ and therefore repeats among the
+$(2d+1)^{m-1}-1$ nonzero vertices, producing a reachable directed cycle.
+This proves all three equivalences and the periodic certificate, whose cycle
+may be chosen simple.
+
+In the injective case the forward subgraph reachable from $B$ is acyclic and
+contains at most $(2d+1)^{m-1}-1$ vertices.  A directed path in it has at
+most $(2d+1)^{m-1}-2$ edges.  Formula
+\eqref{eq:collision-graph-longest-path} then gives
+\eqref{eq:simple-parry-causal-state-bound}.
+\end{proof}
+
+\begin{theorem}[Complete aperture-two trichotomy]
+\label{thm:simple-parry-aperture-two}
+Set
+\[
+c_\beta=t_2+\ind_{\{p\ge3\}}.
+\]
+Then $1\le c_\beta\le d+1$ and
+\[
+Q_2=d(d+1)+c_\beta.
+\]
+Exactly one of the following alternatives holds.
+\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\alph*)}]
+  \item If $c_\beta=d+1$, then $\Fold_{\beta,2}$ is the identity on
+  $\mathcal A_d^2$ and $\ell_{\rm cau}(\beta,2)=1$.
+  \item If $1\le c_\beta<d$, then $\Phi_{\beta,2}$ is injective and
+  $\ell_{\rm cau}(\beta,2)=2$.
+  \item If $c_\beta=d$, then $\Phi_{\beta,2}$ is noninjective.  Its sole
+  nonsingleton path-space fiber is
+  \[
+  \Phi_{\beta,2}(0^{\mathbb Z})
+  =\Phi_{\beta,2}(d^{\mathbb Z})
+  =((0,0))^{\mathbb Z},
+  \]
+  and $\ell_{\rm cau}(\beta,2)=\infty$.
+\end{enumerate}
+For $p=2$ the three cases are determined by $c_\beta=t_2$; for
+$p\ge3$ they are determined by $c_\beta=t_2+1$.  In particular, a binary
+simple-Parry word of order at least three has an identity aperture-two fold
+when $t_2=1$ and exactly the displayed constant branch pair when $t_2=0$.
+\end{theorem}
+
+\begin{proof}
+Put $q=d+1$ and $M=Q_2=dq+c_\beta$.  The formula for $Q_2$ follows directly
+from \eqref{eq:simple-parry-Q}, with the boundary summand $1$ present exactly
+when $2<p$.  Since $t_2\ge1$ when $p=2$, whereas $0\le t_2\le d$ when
+$p\ge3$, the stated range for $c_\beta$ follows.
+
+An edge of $\Gamma_{\beta,2}$ is a pair $(e,f)\in\Delta_d^2$ satisfying
+\begin{equation}
+e+qf\equiv0\pmod M.
+\label{eq:aperture-two-edge-congruence}
+\end{equation}
+The left side has modulus at most
+$d(1+q)=q^2-1<2M$, so it equals $-M$, $0$, or $M$.  If it is zero, then
+$q>|e|$ forces $(e,f)=(0,0)$.  If it is $M$, the bound $e\le d$ forces
+$f=d$, because $f\le d-1$ would give
+$M-qf\ge q+c_\beta>d$; hence $(e,f)=(c_\beta,d)$, which is admissible
+exactly when $c_\beta\le d$.  The case $-M$ is its negative.  Thus the full
+edge set is
+\[
+\{(0,0)\}\quad(c_\beta=d+1),
+\qquad
+\{(0,0),\ \pm(c_\beta,d)\}\quad(c_\beta\le d).
+\]
+
+When $c_\beta=d+1$, one has $Q_2=q^2=|\mathcal A_d^2|$, so every raw
+length-two word is legal and cyclic reduction does nothing.  This proves
+(a).  If $c_\beta<d$, the two nonzero edges cannot be followed by another
+edge, because their terminal vertices are $\pm d$, not $\pm c_\beta$.
+There is a one-output collision but no two-output collision, so
+Theorem~\ref{thm:simple-parry-causal-collision} gives (b).  Finally, when
+$c_\beta=d$, the two nonzero edges are the loops $(d,d)$ and $(-d,-d)$.
+They give precisely the constant difference sequences $\pm d^{\mathbb Z}$.
+The only raw realization of either is the pair
+$\{0^{\mathbb Z},d^{\mathbb Z}\}$, and the common residue is zero in every
+window.  No other nonzero bi-infinite path exists, proving (c) and the fiber
+classification.
+\end{proof}
+
 The graph in Theorem~\ref{thm:simple-parry-causal-collision} is the arithmetic
 specialization of the standard fiber-product collision graph for a sliding
 block code; see \cite{LindMarcus1995,Nasu1995}.  Its substantive role here is

+def _collision_graph(
+    digits: tuple[int, ...], m: int
+) -> dict[tuple[int, ...], tuple[tuple[int, ...], ...]]:
+    """Build the bounded-difference collision graph at aperture ``m``."""
+    if m < 2:
+        raise ValueError("the collision graph requires m>=2")
+    d = digits[0]
+    q = q_sequence(digits, m)
+    modulus = q[m]
+    vertices = product(range(-d, d + 1), repeat=m - 1)
+    adjacency: dict[tuple[int, ...], tuple[tuple[int, ...], ...]] = {}
+    for vertex in vertices:
+        following = []
+        for appended in range(-d, d + 1):
+            weighted = sum(q[j] * vertex[j] for j in range(m - 1))
+            weighted += q[m - 1] * appended
+            if weighted % modulus == 0:
+                following.append(vertex[1:] + (appended,))
+        adjacency[vertex] = tuple(following)
+    return adjacency
+
+
+def _reachable_cycle(
+    adjacency: dict[tuple[int, ...], tuple[tuple[int, ...], ...]],
+    starts: list[tuple[int, ...]],
+) -> tuple[int, ...] | None:
+    """Return the first-coordinate word on a cycle reachable from ``starts``."""
+    color: dict[tuple[int, ...], int] = {}
+    parent: dict[tuple[int, ...], tuple[int, ...]] = {}
+
+    def visit(vertex: tuple[int, ...]) -> tuple[int, ...] | None:
+        color[vertex] = 1
+        for following in adjacency[vertex]:
+            if color.get(following, 0) == 0:
+                parent[following] = vertex
+                witness = visit(following)
+                if witness is not None:
+                    return witness
+            elif color[following] == 1:
+                reverse_cycle = [vertex]
+                while reverse_cycle[-1] != following:
+                    reverse_cycle.append(parent[reverse_cycle[-1]])
+                cycle = tuple(reversed(reverse_cycle))
+                return tuple(state[0] for state in cycle)
+        color[vertex] = 2
+        return None
+
+    for start in starts:
+        if color.get(start, 0) == 0:
+            witness = visit(start)
+            if witness is not None:
+                return witness
+    return None
+
+
+def collision_graph_analysis(
+    digits: tuple[int, ...], m: int
+) -> dict[str, int | bool | tuple[int, ...] | None]:
+    """Return the exact injectivity, causal-depth, and cycle certificates."""
+    adjacency = _collision_graph(digits, m)
+    zero = (0,) * (m - 1)
+    starts = [vertex for vertex in adjacency if vertex[0] != 0]
+    zero_predecessors = [vertex for vertex, targets in adjacency.items() if zero in targets]
+    periodic_witness = _reachable_cycle(adjacency, starts)
+    if periodic_witness is not None and periodic_witness[0] < 0:
+        periodic_witness = tuple(-entry for entry in periodic_witness)
+    injective = periodic_witness is None
+
+    causal_length = None
+    if injective:
+        longest_cache: dict[tuple[int, ...], int] = {}
+
+        def longest_path(vertex: tuple[int, ...]) -> int:
+            if vertex not in longest_cache:
+                longest_cache[vertex] = max(
+                    (1 + longest_path(target) for target in adjacency[vertex]),
+                    default=0,
+                )
+            return longest_cache[vertex]
+
+        causal_length = 1 + max(longest_path(start) for start in starts)
+
+    return {
+        "injective": injective,
+        "causal_length": causal_length,
+        "periodic_witness": periodic_witness,
+        "zero_predecessor_is_unique": zero_predecessors == [zero],
+        "state_bound": len(adjacency) - 1,
+    }
+
+
+def aperture_two_claims(
+    digits: tuple[int, ...],
+) -> dict[str, int | str | tuple[int, ...] | None]:
+    """Classify aperture two by the second-digit boundary parameter."""
+    if len(digits) < 2:
+        raise ValueError("the aperture-two classification requires Parry order p>=2")
+    d = digits[0]
+    boundary = digits[1] + (1 if len(digits) > 2 else 0)
+    analysis = collision_graph_analysis(digits, 2)
+    if boundary == d + 1:
+        regime = "local_bijection"
+    elif boundary == d:
+        regime = "constant_branch_pair"
+    else:
+        regime = "two_output_inverse"
+    return {
+        "boundary_parameter": boundary,
+        "regime": regime,
+        "causal_length": analysis["causal_length"],
+        "periodic_witness": analysis["periodic_witness"],
+    }
+

+\begin{corollary}[Causal completeness and periodic detection]
+\label{cor:simple-parry-causal-completeness}
+Under the preceding hypotheses, for every $m\ge2$ the following are
+equivalent:
+\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\roman*)}]
+  \item $\Phi_{\beta,m}$ is injective;
+  \item $\ell_{\rm cau}(\beta,m)<\infty$;
+  \item no directed cycle of $\Gamma_{\beta,m}$ is reachable from $B$.
+\end{enumerate}
+If these conditions hold, then
+\begin{equation}
+1\le \ell_{\rm cau}(\beta,m)
+\le (2d+1)^{m-1}-1.
+\label{eq:simple-parry-causal-state-bound}
+\end{equation}
+If they fail, there are distinct periodic raw points with the same image and
+with common period at most $(2d+1)^{m-1}-1$.  Thus injectivity in this class
+can be decided by a finite forward cycle search, and every failure has a
+bounded periodic certificate.
+\end{corollary}
+
+\begin{proof}
+The recurrence \eqref{eq:simple-parry-Q} gives $Q_1=d+1$ and shows
+inductively that $Q_n>Q_{n-1}$: before the terminal index there is the
+additional summand $1$, while at and after that index the positive term
+$t_pQ_{n-p}$ accompanies $dQ_{n-1}$.  In particular, $Q_m>d$.
+
+Let $\mathbf0=(0,\ldots,0)\in\Delta_d^{m-1}$.  If an edge
+$v\to\mathbf0$ exists, the overlap conditions give
+$v_1=\cdots=v_{m-2}=0$, and the edge congruence reduces to
+$v_0\equiv0\pmod{Q_m}$.  Since $|v_0|\le d<Q_m$, necessarily
+$v=\mathbf0$.  Hence the zero vertex has the zero vertex as its unique
+predecessor and is not reachable from $B$.
+
+If $\Phi_{\beta,m}$ is injective, the last assertion of
+Theorem~\ref{thm:simple-parry-causal-collision} now gives a finite causal
+inverse.  The converse is immediate because a decoder recovers every raw
+coordinate.  A directed cycle reachable from $B$ cannot contain
+$\mathbf0$; repeating its first-coordinate labels gives a nonzero periodic
+difference sequence and hence, by taking positive and negative parts, two
+distinct periodic raw points with the same image.  Conversely, from any
+nonzero bi-infinite collision path, shift to a vertex in $B$.  Its forward
+path avoids $\mathbf0$ and therefore repeats among the
+$(2d+1)^{m-1}-1$ nonzero vertices, producing a reachable directed cycle.
+This proves all three equivalences and the periodic certificate, whose cycle
+may be chosen simple.
+
+In the injective case the forward subgraph reachable from $B$ is acyclic and
+contains at most $(2d+1)^{m-1}-1$ vertices.  A directed path in it has at
+most $(2d+1)^{m-1}-2$ edges.  Formula
+\eqref{eq:collision-graph-longest-path} then gives
+\eqref{eq:simple-parry-causal-state-bound}.
+\end{proof}
+
+\begin{theorem}[Complete aperture-two trichotomy]
+\label{thm:simple-parry-aperture-two}
+Set
+\[
+c_\beta=t_2+\ind_{\{p\ge3\}}.
+\]
+Then $1\le c_\beta\le d+1$ and
+\[
+Q_2=d(d+1)+c_\beta.
+\]
+Exactly one of the following alternatives holds.
+\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\alph*)}]
+  \item If $c_\beta=d+1$, then $\Fold_{\beta,2}$ is the identity on
+  $\mathcal A_d^2$ and $\ell_{\rm cau}(\beta,2)=1$.
+  \item If $1\le c_\beta<d$, then $\Phi_{\beta,2}$ is injective and
+  $\ell_{\rm cau}(\beta,2)=2$.
+  \item If $c_\beta=d$, then $\Phi_{\beta,2}$ is noninjective.  Its sole
+  nonsingleton path-space fiber is
+  \[
+  \Phi_{\beta,2}(0^{\mathbb Z})
+  =\Phi_{\beta,2}(d^{\mathbb Z})
+  =((0,0))^{\mathbb Z},
+  \]
+  and $\ell_{\rm cau}(\beta,2)=\infty$.
+\end{enumerate}
+For $p=2$ the three cases are determined by $c_\beta=t_2$; for
+$p\ge3$ they are determined by $c_\beta=t_2+1$.  In particular, a binary
+simple-Parry word of order at least three has an identity aperture-two fold
+when $t_2=1$ and exactly the displayed constant branch pair when $t_2=0$.
+\end{theorem}
+
+\begin{proof}
+Put $q=d+1$ and $M=Q_2=dq+c_\beta$.  The formula for $Q_2$ follows directly
+from \eqref{eq:simple-parry-Q}, with the boundary summand $1$ present exactly
+when $2<p$.  Since $t_2\ge1$ when $p=2$, whereas $0\le t_2\le d$ when
+$p\ge3$, the stated range for $c_\beta$ follows.
+
+An edge of $\Gamma_{\beta,2}$ is a pair $(e,f)\in\Delta_d^2$ satisfying
+\begin{equation}
+e+qf\equiv0\pmod M.
+\label{eq:aperture-two-edge-congruence}
+\end{equation}
+The left side has modulus at most
+$d(1+q)=q^2-1<2M$, so it equals $-M$, $0$, or $M$.  If it is zero, then
+$q>|e|$ forces $(e,f)=(0,0)$.  If it is $M$, the bound $e\le d$ forces
+$f=d$, because $f\le d-1$ would give
+$M-qf\ge q+c_\beta>d$; hence $(e,f)=(c_\beta,d)$, which is admissible
+exactly when $c_\beta\le d$.  The case $-M$ is its negative.  Thus the full
+edge set is
+\[
+\{(0,0)\}\quad(c_\beta=d+1),
+\qquad
+\{(0,0),\ \pm(c_\beta,d)\}\quad(c_\beta\le d).
+\]
+
+When $c_\beta=d+1$, one has $Q_2=q^2=|\mathcal A_d^2|$, so every raw
+length-two word is legal and cyclic reduction does nothing.  This proves
+(a).  If $c_\beta<d$, the two nonzero edges cannot be followed by another
+edge, because their terminal vertices are $\pm d$, not $\pm c_\beta$.
+There is a one-output collision but no two-output collision, so
+Theorem~\ref{thm:simple-parry-causal-collision} gives (b).  Finally, when
+$c_\beta=d$, the two nonzero edges are the loops $(d,d)$ and $(-d,-d)$.
+They give precisely the constant difference sequences $\pm d^{\mathbb Z}$.
+The only raw realization of either is the pair
+$\{0^{\mathbb Z},d^{\mathbb Z}\}$, and the common residue is zero in every
+window.  No other nonzero bi-infinite path exists, proving (c) and the fiber
+classification.
+\end{proof}
+

 specialization of the standard fiber-product collision graph for a sliding
 block code; see \cite{LindMarcus1995,Nasu1995}.  Its substantive role here is

+def _collision_graph(
+    digits: tuple[int, ...], m: int
+) -> dict[tuple[int, ...], tuple[tuple[int, ...], ...]]:
+    """Build the bounded-difference collision graph at aperture ``m``."""
+    if m < 2:
+        raise ValueError("the collision graph requires m>=2")
+    d = digits[0]
+    q = q_sequence(digits, m)
+    modulus = q[m]
+    vertices = product(range(-d, d + 1), repeat=m - 1)
+    adjacency: dict[tuple[int, ...], tuple[tuple[int, ...], ...]] = {}
+    for vertex in vertices:
+        following = []
+        for appended in range(-d, d + 1):
+            weighted = sum(q[j] * vertex[j] for j in range(m - 1))
+            weighted += q[m - 1] * appended
+            if weighted % modulus == 0:
+                following.append(vertex[1:] + (appended,))
+        adjacency[vertex] = tuple(following)
+    return adjacency
+
+
+def _reachable_cycle(
+    adjacency: dict[tuple[int, ...], tuple[tuple[int, ...], ...]],
+    starts: list[tuple[int, ...]],
+) -> tuple[int, ...] | None:
+    """Return the first-coordinate word on a cycle reachable from ``starts``."""
+    color: dict[tuple[int, ...], int] = {}
+    parent: dict[tuple[int, ...], tuple[int, ...]] = {}
+
+    def visit(vertex: tuple[int, ...]) -> tuple[int, ...] | None:
+        color[vertex] = 1
+        for following in adjacency[vertex]:
+            if color.get(following, 0) == 0:
+                parent[following] = vertex
+                witness = visit(following)
+                if witness is not None:
+                    return witness
+            elif color[following] == 1:
+                reverse_cycle = [vertex]
+                while reverse_cycle[-1] != following:
+                    reverse_cycle.append(parent[reverse_cycle[-1]])
+                cycle = tuple(reversed(reverse_cycle))
+                return tuple(state[0] for state in cycle)
+        color[vertex] = 2
+        return None
+
+    for start in starts:
+        if color.get(start, 0) == 0:
+            witness = visit(start)
+            if witness is not None:
+                return witness
+    return None
+
+
+def collision_graph_analysis(
+    digits: tuple[int, ...], m: int
+) -> dict[str, int | bool | tuple[int, ...] | None]:
+    """Return the exact injectivity, causal-depth, and cycle certificates."""
+    adjacency = _collision_graph(digits, m)
+    zero = (0,) * (m - 1)
+    starts = [vertex for vertex in adjacency if vertex[0] != 0]
+    zero_predecessors = [vertex for vertex, targets in adjacency.items() if zero in targets]
+    periodic_witness = _reachable_cycle(adjacency, starts)
+    if periodic_witness is not None and periodic_witness[0] < 0:
+        periodic_witness = tuple(-entry for entry in periodic_witness)
+    injective = periodic_witness is None
+
+    causal_length = None
+    if injective:
+        longest_cache: dict[tuple[int, ...], int] = {}
+
+        def longest_path(vertex: tuple[int, ...]) -> int:
+            if vertex not in longest_cache:
+                longest_cache[vertex] = max(
+                    (1 + longest_path(target) for target in adjacency[vertex]),
+                    default=0,
+                )
+            return longest_cache[vertex]
+
+        causal_length = 1 + max(longest_path(start) for start in starts)
+
+    return {
+        "injective": injective,
+        "causal_length": causal_length,
+        "periodic_witness": periodic_witness,
+        "zero_predecessor_is_unique": zero_predecessors == [zero],
+        "state_bound": len(adjacency) - 1,
+    }
+
+
+def aperture_two_claims(
+    digits: tuple[int, ...],
+) -> dict[str, int | str | tuple[int, ...] | None]:
+    """Classify aperture two by the second-digit boundary parameter."""
+    if len(digits) < 2:
+        raise ValueError("the aperture-two classification requires Parry order p>=2")
+    d = digits[0]
+    boundary = digits[1] + (1 if len(digits) > 2 else 0)
+    analysis = collision_graph_analysis(digits, 2)
+    if boundary == d + 1:
+        regime = "local_bijection"
+    elif boundary == d:
+        regime = "constant_branch_pair"
+    else:
+        regime = "two_output_inverse"
+    return {
+        "boundary_parameter": boundary,
+        "regime": regime,
+        "causal_length": analysis["causal_length"],
+        "periodic_witness": analysis["periodic_witness"],
+    }
+
